extName.description: The extension's name, as Chrome shows it. Not translated: it is the product name.

ext_error_settingsTooLarge.message: These settings are too large for Chrome to sync. Shorten the longest command and try again

ext_export_excludedUnsaved.message: Unsaved changes were not included in the export.

ext_export_nothingSaved.message: No settings have been saved yet. Save first, then export.

ext_field_claudeInput_placeholder.message: !gh issue view {number}, or: summarize this issue

ext_field_claudeInputs_help.message: — delivered in order; ! lines run in claude's shell mode

ext_field_claudeInputs_hint.message: ! lines are typed into claude's shell mode so they really run as commands — consecutive ones go in as a single line joined with ;, each behind a banner. On Warp that typing needs the Accessibility permission. A single plain-text input, with nothing else in the list, skips typing entirely and becomes claude's opening message — that additionally needs the command to end in a bare claude.

ext_field_claudeInputs_warn.message: ⚠ The command doesn't start claude, so these inputs won't be delivered

ext_migration_badge.message: ● Your saved buttons predate the current presets — review

ext_migration_hint_reviewOnly.message: Dismissing this marks your settings as reviewed — press $ARG1$ afterwards.

ext_migration_hint_selected.message: $ARG1$ of $ARG2$ selected. Applying fills the form; press $ARG3$ to store it.

ext_migration_intro_nothingSafe.message: Nothing here can be rewritten safely, but these commands still use the old form:

ext_migration_intro_nothingToDo.message: Nothing to change — your commands are already current. Press $ARG1$ to mark them as reviewed.

ext_migration_markedReviewed.message: Marked as reviewed. Press $ARG1$ to keep your commands as they are.

ext_migration_v1_customNote.message: This command was edited, so it is left exactly as it is — z {repo} is not its first clause, and rewriting it safely would mean parsing the shell. Replace the leading jump with {cd} yourself if you want the same fallbacks.

ext_migration_v1_describe.message: The command opens with {cd} instead of z {repo}. With no repository base folder set in the Terminal Checkout app this runs exactly what it runs today; if you have set one, z failing now falls back to that folder and clones the repository when it is not there.

ext_migration_v1_prefixDescribe.message: Your command continues after the jump. With a base folder set, a failed z now lands in the repository folder underneath it, or in a fresh clone — make sure the rest of this command is safe to run there before accepting it.

ext_migration_v2_describe.message: This generation adds separate buttons for PR and issue list pages; existing commands are not rewritten.

ext_migration_v3_describe.message: The list pages renamed {pr}/{issue} to the {number} the detail pages already use; a saved list button still holding the old names would stop rendering.

ext_reorder_tooltip.message: Drag, or use the ↑↓ keys, to reorder

ext_section_backup_help1.message: Settings (PR, issue, and repository buttons, and the main branch) are stored in Chrome's account-synced area (storage.sync). This extension has a fixed ID (the manifest key), so any two Chrome profiles signed in to the same Google account with "Extensions" enabled in sync settings share these settings automatically. Export and import are for moving settings without an account, or for keeping a file backup.

ext_section_backup_help2.message: Export downloads the saved settings as a file; import only fills in the form — nothing takes effect until you press $ARG1$.

ext_section_backup_help3.message: The file also records which generation of the presets it was written against. Importing an older backup offers the same update notice as stored settings do — and since a file may cover only part of your settings, the notice then reviews the whole form, not just the keys the file carried. A backup written by a newer extension is refused rather than half-read; update the extension first.

ext_section_backup_title.message: backup — export, import, account sync

ext_section_issue_claudeHelp.message: A claude input that starts with ! is typed into claude's shell mode, so the command really runs in that session — the default preset uses gh to put the issue body, its comments and the issues that mention it in front of claude. Consecutive ! inputs are typed as one line.

ext_section_issue_help.message: Buttons that sit next to the status badge (Open/Closed) on an issue page (up to $ARG1$). They are configured separately from the PR buttons, and on an issue page clicking the extension icon runs the first button here. Reordering (drag ⠿, or ↑ ↓) and duplicating work just like they do for PR buttons.

ext_section_issue_variables.message: Available variables: {cd} (move into the repository — filled in by the app) {repo} {owner} {number} (issue number, digits only) {main} — an issue has no PR branch, so the {branch} family and {base} are unavailable.

ext_section_issueList_claudeHelp.message: The default list button opens claude and types !gh issue view {number} --comments into claude's shell mode.

ext_section_issueList_help.message: Buttons for an issue list page (up to $ARG1$). Configure the command that each selected issue will run in its own terminal session.

ext_section_issueList_variables.message: Available variables: {cd} (move into the repository — filled in by the app) {repo} {number} (issue number, digits only) — a list page has no {branch} or {base}.

ext_section_main_help.message: How {main} is resolved: per-repository override → detected from the page → the default below. Detection reads the base branch on a PR page, and the repository default branch on repository and issue pages — the setting below is the fallback for when detection fails. To always use the branch a PR will actually be merged into, use {base}, which skips both the override and the default.

ext_section_pr_help1.message: Buttons that sit next to the branch name on a PR page (up to $ARG1$). $ARG2$ is what the button shows — a single emoji, several of them (🌳🤖), or a short name (Review, WT). $ARG3$ appears on hover, and picking a preset fills the card with that template.

ext_section_pr_help2.message: Drag the ⠿ handle on the left of a card, or use the ↑ ↓ keys, to reorder — this is the order the buttons appear in on GitHub, and clicking the extension icon runs the first one. $ARG1$ is for making another button like an existing one — the copy's tooltip gets a number such as (1) appended.

ext_section_pr_migrationHelp.message: Rewrites of presets we shipped are pre-checked. A command you customized is offered unchecked and marked as a behavior change: only its leading jump is replaced, and the rest of it will now run wherever the new entry clause lands. Every preset starts with {cd}. With no base folder set it is just z {repo}; with one, it falls back to that folder and clones the repository when it isn't there — so a button works even on a repository you have never opened locally.

ext_section_pr_variables.message: Available variables: {cd} (move into the repository — the app fills this in from its repository base folder setting, so it works on every page) {repo} {owner} {number} (PR number, digits only) {branch} (head — the branch being merged) {base} (base — the branch it merges into) {main} {branch_underbar} (branch with / replaced by _)

ext_section_prList_help.message: Buttons for a PR list page (up to $ARG1$). Configure the command that each selected PR will run in its own terminal session.

ext_section_prList_variables.message: Available variables: {cd} (move into the repository — filled in by the app) {repo} {number} (PR number, digits only) — a list page has no {branch} or {base}; use gh pr checkout {number} to resolve the branch locally.

ext_section_repo_help.message: Buttons that sit next to the repository name in the header of a repository page (code, issue list, Actions, and so on) — up to $ARG1$. Unlike the PR and issue buttons these look like GitHub's green action button, so a name such as $ARG2$ suits the $ARG3$ better than an emoji. On GitHub pages that are neither a PR nor an issue, clicking the extension icon runs the first button here.

ext_section_repo_variables.message: Available variables: {cd} (move into the repository — filled in by the app) {repo} {owner} {main} — a repository page has neither a PR or issue number nor a branch, so {number}, the {branch} family, and {base} are unavailable. {main} is resolved from the repository default branch GitHub embeds in the page — a master repository comes out right without an override.

ext_section_update_title.message: update — saved commands versus the current presets

ext_status_reset.message: Reset to defaults. Press $ARG1$ to apply.

ext_status_savedWithPendingEdits.message: Settings saved. Changes made since then are not saved yet.
